title: Optimized Protocol for Assessing SUMOylation in Capsella rubella
author: Dong, Hu, et al.
materials: Refer to “key resources table” and “materials and equipment” for the lists of reagents and equipment.

steps.title: Prepare 1% fixative buffer
steps.instruction: Dilute 10× PBS to 1× PBS with sterile ddH₂O and add 37% formaldehyde to a final concentration of 1% to make 100 mL fixative buffer. Prepare fresh, seal the container to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Fix seedlings under vacuum
steps.instruction: Harvest DEX‑treated seedlings, wrap in a single layer of Miracloth, and infiltrate with the fixative buffer in a 50 mL beaker under vacuum (minimum 100 mbar) for 15 min; release the vacuum slowly. Then add 6.25 mL of 2 M glycine (final 125 mM) under vacuum for an additional 5 min to quench the fixation.

steps.title: Rinse, dry, and weigh tissue
steps.instruction: Rinse the fixed seedlings three times with ddH₂O, pat dry with laboratory tissues, and record the wet weight.

steps.title: Pre‑cool equipment in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Place the mortar, pestle, 15 mL Falcon tubes, and spatula in liquid nitrogen until completely chilled.

steps.title: Grind tissue to fine powder
steps.instruction: Grind approximately 1.0 g of the frozen seedlings in liquid nitrogen 2–3 times using the pre‑cooled mortar and pestle until a fine powder is obtained.

steps.title: Extract proteins with buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the powder to a pre‑cooled 15 mL conical tube with a pre‑cooled spatula, add 2.5 mL protein extraction buffer (2.5×V; contains N‑ethylmaleimide), gently invert to mix, then place tubes on a rotator and extract at 40 rpm for 1 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Clarify extract by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C. Centrifuge the extracts at ~15,000 rcf, 4 °C for 10 min. Collect the supernatant and split into two 2.0 mL Eppendorf tubes (~1.5 mL each) on ice.

steps.title: Second spin and repeat until clear
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the split samples again at ~15,000 rcf, 4 °C for 5 min. Transfer the clear supernatant to a new 2.0 mL Eppendorf tube on ice. Repeat the split‑centrifuge steps (previous step) until the supernatant is clear.

steps.title: Prepare input sample for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Aliquot 50 µL of the clarified lysate, add 50 µL 2× SDS loading buffer, and boil at 100 °C for 5 min. Open the tube lid carefully after boiling.

steps.title: Store input samples
steps.instruction: Store the boiled input samples at –20 °C until analysis.

description: Conjugation of small ubiquitin-related modifier (SUMO) to the proteins provides the plants with a fast and dynamic regulatory mechanism to cope with environmental fluctuations and intrinsic developmental clues (Mukhopadhyay and Dasso, 2007). Similar to ubiquitin, SUMO becomes covalently attached to lysyl ε-amino groups in the target proteins by the action of a dedicated enzymatic cascade (Miura and Hasegawa, 2010). Upon conjugation, SUMOylation usher in profound impact on the target protein, including the way they interact with other proteins and nucleic acids, stability and subcellular localization (Mukhopadhyay and Dasso, 2007). Interestingly, SUMOylation is a highly dynamic and reversible process as the SUMOs can be trimmed off by specific cysteine proteases in developmental-context dependent manner (Miura and Hasegawa, 2010). All these features make detection of SUMOylation a challenge in analyzing the biochemical property of a protein of interest. Recently, we found that changes in regulatory region(s) of the CrIND gene compared to Arabidopsis lead to expressional expansion of CrIND from the valve margin to the valves in the cap, leading to the development of a heart-shaped fruit (Dong et al., 2019). In the valve tips, CrIND directly activates the expression of CrTAA1 and CrYUC9, which in turn results in auxin maxima that affect cell anisotropic growth behavior in the valves and establish the heart (Dong et al., 2019). The CrIND protein function is fine-tuned at the post-translational level by SUMOylation as mutations in HTB, which encodes SUMO proteases, destabilize CrIND by SUMOylation (Dong et al., 2020). CrIND encodes a b-HLH transcription factor and exhibits a tissue specific expression pattern (Liljegren et al., 2004; Dong et al., 2019). In addition, over-expression of CrIND results in dramatic changes in the organ polarity and thus brings about plant lethality at the seedling stage (Moubayidin and Østergaard, 2014).
